subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: Paradigm Shifts: When the Whole Framework Changes
description: Learn Paradigm Shifts: When the Whole Framework Changes in one minute.

hook.text: For 1,400 years, Earth was the center of the universe. Then Copernicus moved the Sun to the center. Same sky, new truth.

buildup.text: Thomas Kuhn: science doesn't progress smoothly.

discovery.text: A paradigm is a framework of assumptions. Normal science works within it. Anomalies pile up until the framework breaks.

twist.text: During a shift, old and new paradigms are 'incommensurable' — they don't share enough assumptions to compare directly.

climax.text: Copernicus, Darwin, Einstein, plate tectonics – each required scientists to abandon deep assumptions, not just add.

punchline.text: Sometimes progress means changing the question, not the answer.

quiz.question: What is a paradigm shift according to Thomas Kuhn?
options: A revolutionary change in the fundamental framework of scientific assumptions
A political change in science funding

details.summary: Thomas Kuhn argued that science does not progress smoothly but through revolutionary paradigm shifts where the entire framework of understanding changes. The shift from Newtonian to Einsteinian physics is a classic example.
details.whyItMatters: Paradigm shifts show that scientific truth is not permanent. What counts as knowledge depends on the reigning paradigm, which can be overthrown by evidence it cannot accommodate.
takeaways: Normal science works within an accepted paradigm
Anomalies accumulate until a crisis triggers revolution
New paradigms are incommensurable with old ones

faq.question: What triggers a scientific paradigm shift according to Thomas Kuhn?
faq.answer: Anomalies that the current paradigm cannot explain accumulate over time. When enough anomalies pile up and a compelling alternative framework emerges, a crisis develops. If the new paradigm explains more, the scientific community shifts.

faq.question: What does Kuhn mean by saying paradigms are incommensurable?
faq.answer: Scientists in different paradigms may use the same words with different meanings and consider different problems important. This makes direct comparison difficult because the frameworks define reality differently, not just explain it differently.
